## Standards and Methodology Embedded

All documents reference and align with:

### General Standards
- **ATA iSpec 2200** - Information Standards
- **ATA 100** - Chapter 10 Parking, Mooring, Storage
- **SAE ARP4754A** - Systems Development Guidelines
- **SAE ARP4761** - Safety Assessment Methods
- **MIL-STD-881** - Work Breakdown Structures

### H2/Cryogenic Standards
- **SAE AS6968** - Hydrogen Aircraft Systems
- **NFPA 2** - Hydrogen Technologies Code
- **ISO 11114-4** - H2 Material Compatibility
- **ISO 13984** - Liquid Hydrogen Tanks
- **ISO 20421-1** - Cryogenic Vessels

### Safety & Certification
- **DO-178C** - Software Assurance
- **DO-254** - Hardware Assurance
- **IEC 61508** - Functional Safety
- **ATEX 2014/34/EU** - Explosive Atmospheres
- **IECEx** - International Ex Certification

## Key Features of the Framework

### 1. H2 Safety Focus

Special emphasis on hydrogen safety with:
- Dedicated H2 safety subsystem category (40-49)
- H2 detection, venting, alarm, ESD, monitoring
- LEL (Lower Explosive Limit) thresholds and response times
- ATEX/IECEx certification requirements
- Material compatibility (ISO 11114-4)

### 2. Cryogenic Systems

LH2-specific considerations:
- Cryogenic subsystem category (50-59)
- Tank interfaces, insulation, valves
- Boiloff management, thermal protection
- Temperature range: -253°C to ambient
- Multi-Layer Insulation (MLI) specifications

### 3. BWB Configuration

BWB-specific adaptations:
- Dedicated BWB subsystem category (60-69)
- Geometry-specific tiedown and mooring
- Wide-body load distribution
- Ground clearance management
- Unconventional CG considerations

### 4. Safety Architecture

Safety-critical system handling:
- Design Assurance Levels (DAL A-E)
- Fail-safe design principles
- Redundancy requirements
- Hazard traceability
- Requirements verification methods

### 5. Product Breakdown Structure

Hierarchical component organization:
- PBS methodology (MIL-STD-881)
- Component-level traceability
- Part number management
- Supplier analysis
- Cost tracking

## How to Complete a Stub Document

### Step-by-Step Process

1. **Open the stub document** (e.g., `10-00-13-41A_H2_Venting_Subsystem.md`)

2. **Open the appropriate template**:
   - For subsystems: `subsystems-templates/subsystem-spec-template.md`
   - For components: `subsystems-templates/component-spec-template.md`
   - For PBS: `subsystems-templates/pbs-template.md`

3. **Copy template content** into the stub document (replace stub content)

4. **Fill in all bracketed placeholders** `[...]` with actual values:
   - Document ID, title, revision, date
   - Subsystem type, subsystem ID, parent system
   - Functional description, operational modes
   - Component lists, interfaces
   - Requirements, hazards, standards

5. **Complete all applicable sections**:
   - For H2 systems: Fill Section 12 (H2/Cryo Specific Considerations)
   - For BWB systems: Fill Section 13 (BWB-Specific Considerations)
   - For safety-critical: Complete Section 8 (Safety Features) in detail

6. **Add cross-references**:
   - Link to parent system architecture document
   - Link to related subsystems
   - Link to requirements (10-00-03_Requirements)
   - Link to safety analysis (10-00-02_Safety)

7. **Create architecture diagrams** (if applicable):
   - Use architecture-diagram-template.md as guide
   - Create SVG files in ASSETS/ subfolder
   - Reference diagrams in document

8. **Update document status**:
   - Change status from STUB to DRAFT
   - Add author name and date
   - Increment revision if updating existing draft

9. **Update 00_INDEX.md**:
   - Change status from STUB to DRAFT in index table

10. **Submit for review**:
    - Technical review by SME
    - Approval process per document control procedures

## Quality Checklist for Completed Documents

Before marking a document as FOR_REVIEW or APPROVED, verify:

### Content Completeness
- [ ] All sections filled (or marked N/A with justification)
- [ ] No `[placeholder]` or `TBD` entries without explanation
- [ ] Component lists complete with part numbers (or TBD with plan)
- [ ] Interface IDs assigned and documented
- [ ] Requirements traceability table populated

### H2/Cryo/BWB Specific (if applicable)
- [ ] Section 12 (H2/Cryo) completed for H2/cryo subsystems
- [ ] Section 13 (BWB) completed for BWB-specific subsystems
- [ ] ATEX/IECEx certifications identified where required
- [ ] Material compatibility addressed (ISO 11114-4)

### Cross-References
- [ ] Links to parent system architecture work
- [ ] Links to related subsystems work
- [ ] Links to requirements database functional
- [ ] Links to safety analysis functional

### Standards Compliance
- [ ] Applicable standards listed in Section 15
- [ ] Design complies with cited standards (or deviations noted)
- [ ] Safety-critical systems have DAL level assigned

### Document Control
- [ ] Document ID matches filename
- [ ] Revision letter matches document control table
- [ ] Revision history table populated
- [ ] AI generation note present
- [ ] Status field accurate (DRAFT/FOR_REVIEW/APPROVED)
